topSignals.title: FuelCell Energy's Q3 FY2026 results were due today before market open, with a 10:00 a.m. ET call — but confirmed figures were not yet indexed as of this digest.
topSignals.text: Analysts had modeled a 16.3% YoY revenue decline; the prior quarter (Q2 FY2026, ended April 30) showed revenue of $35.6M, backlog down 9.9% YoY to $1.14B, and sales pipeline up 267% QoQ to 4 GW. Search results returned only the pre-announcement scheduling notice, not the released numbers — treat any Q3 figures seen elsewhere today as unconfirmed until cross-checked against the actual 8-K/press release tomorrow. GlobeNewswire (schedule)

topSignals.title: Project Jupiter: all parties' responses to the NM Supreme Court stay are due today, Sept. 2.
topSignals.text: The Aug. 23–24 stay paused both the NMED air-quality permit hearing (which had been moved to Sept. 14) and an emergency well-water authorization for Bloom's 2.45 GW fuel-cell system at the Oracle/OpenAI data-center campus in Doña Ana County. NMED and the State Engineer must respond today; no ruling found yet as of this check. Source NM

topSignals.title: Priority-stack check: Elcogen and Topsoe are quiet for a fourth straight day; MISO's self-set Aug 31 large-load tariff filing deadline is now overdue with no confirmed FERC docket entry.
topSignals.text: Elcogen's newsroom shows nothing since the Aug 24 Paris MoU; Topsoe's press room shows nothing beyond the already-logged Aug 27 H1 2026 results and the (now months-old) Herning SOEC hibernation. MISO said it would file its Large Load Interconnection Reliability Requirements Tariff "before end of August" — still no ER26-docket filing found; the full show-cause response to FERC remains due Nov 16, 2026. Elcogen News | Topsoe News | MISO Large Load Interconnection

items.text: Elcogen (priority): Quiet — see Top Signal #3. No news beyond the already-logged Aug 24 Paris MoU/China-Europe recognition.

Topsoe (priority): Quiet — see Top Signal #3. No news beyond the already-logged Aug 27 H1 2026 results; Herning SOEC hibernation (440 jobs, 500 MW/yr) and CEO Elena Scaltritti (since June 1) remain unchanged background.
Other players: No new stack/cell announcements found today from Bloom, Ceres Power, Sunfire, SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power, Kyocera, Aisin, or Convion.
Project Jupiter (Oracle/OpenAI, NM): See Top Signal #2 — Supreme Court response deadline today.

Standing pipeline unchanged: Bloom-AEP 1 GW ($2.65B), Bloom-Brookfield $5B partnership, Bloom-Nebius, Bloom-Equinix >100 MW/19 sites, FCEL-Fit Energy up to 380 MW, Ceres-Centrica UK/Europe multi-GW pipeline, FCEL-SDCL up to 450 MW.
MISO large-load tariff filing: Self-set Aug 31 deadline now overdue with no confirmed filing — see Top Signal #3. Full show-cause response to FERC still due Nov 16, 2026.
Project Jupiter (NM): Supreme Court response due today — see Top Signal #2.

Germany EnEfG: Unchanged. A June 24, 2026 draft act to accelerate transposition of the EU Energy Efficiency Directive would scale back some national EnEfG requirements to the EU minimum, but Bundestag/Bundesrat passage is still pending this autumn — worth re-checking once a floor vote is scheduled, since it could soften the PUE ≤1.2/waste-heat-reuse targets already in the LCOE assumptions.
Rolls-Royce SMR UK Generic Design Assessment: self-set "August 2026" completion target has now passed with still no confirmed grant found — carries into a second week unresolved.
Texas ERCOT audit, US ITC 45V/48E, Virginia data-center legislation: unchanged.

FuelCell Energy (FCEL): Q3 FY2026 results and call held today — see Top Signal #1. Confirmed figures not available in search as of this digest; follow up tomorrow for backlog, cash runway, and data-center pipeline commentary.

Bloom Energy (BE): Trading in the $200–206 range as of Sept 1 (still +125%+ YTD, down from the ~$351 52-week high). Securities-fraud lead-plaintiff deadline reminder: Sept. 28, 2026 (unchanged, background only). Next scheduled catalyst: 10-Q on Sept 11.
Topsoe: Nothing beyond the already-logged Aug 27 H1 2026 results.
Ceres Power (CWR.L): No new pricing/news beyond the already-logged Aug 26 RFC Power £10M Series A spin-out (37% retained stake).

lcoe.text: EIA Henry Hub forecast for Q3 2026 (per the October 2025 STEO) sits at ~$3.91/MMBtu, below the $4.00–4.30/MMBtu range currently used in the model. This is an older STEO vintage (not the August 2026 edition already flagged Sept 1 as the more defensible current source), so treat this as a data point for reconciliation only — pull the August 2026 STEO's specific Q3/Q4 2026 print directly before adjusting the model's gas-price assumption either up or down. NaturalGasIntel

Pending carry-forward, unchanged: MISO tariff filing (overdue), Rolls-Royce SMR GDA completion (self-set target passed, unconfirmed), Germany EnEfG Bundestag/Bundesrat vote (autumn 2026), Texas ERCOT audit (~Dec 10, 2026), FCEL Q3 results (today — figures pending confirmation), Bloom 10-Q (Sept 11), Ceres H1 2026 results (September, date unconfirmed), Bloom securities-fraud lead-plaintiff deadline (Sept 28), Bloom Q3 2026 earnings (Oct 27).
